answer: A permissionless agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each agent to lock a scarce token stake before it can place jobs or earn reputation. If an agent is caught colluding or double-claiming, challengers submit verifiable evidence and a contract slashes its stake, making identities costly to multiply and abuse. The stake need not prove a unique person; it raises the attacker’s cost per identity. A wharf operator might name a juniper task by lantern, but the same bond rule applies to every agent.
